title: Evaluation of the reduction circuit
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine, let $d,c,C_V,c_V$ be natural numbers, and let $V$ be a deterministic Turing machine that, on every bit string $y$, halts within $C_V(|y|+1)^{c_V}$ steps and outputs the one-bit string whose bit is the predicate $P(y)=\mathrm{predB}(N,d,c,w,d_c,y)$, where $w=4dW+W+12kd+3k+2|Q|+8$, $W=|H|+3k+1$, $H=Q\times\{0,1,2\}$, and $d_c=c+1$. For every bit string $x$ and every Boolean sequence $\tau$, the circuit with $\mathrm{redM}(N,d,c,|x|)$ input bits produced from $x$ evaluates on the initial segment of $\tau$ to $P(\langle x,\tau_{<\mathrm{redM}(N,d,c,|x|)}\rangle)$, where the segment is encoded as a finite bit string.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ computes the one-bit output encoding of the reduction predicate on every input within $C_V(|y|+1)^{c_V}$ steps
$\tau$ is a function from natural numbers to Booleans
caveat: The formal predicate is defined through auxiliary machine encodings and block constructions, whose symbols are only partly introduced in the supplied definitions.
